I just moved and need to switch banks. What should I be looking for and/or avoiding?
Be sure your bank doesn't charge a fee if your account drops below a minimum balance.

I've been a member of a couple different credit unions and definitely second the motion. Membership perks like regular dividends and rewards for making purchases with your debit card are very nice. They also tend to network with other CUs so you can find ATMs easily, even in places you're not a member of. Way fewer nonsense fees in my experience, too. Not all CUs are equal though, so definitely do your research ahead of time.

Alternately, get into Bitcoin and be your own bank! There's still a long way to go before you can live just on BTC, but it is picking up steam. I think in 5-10 years it will be a lot more viable. If you can spare a portion of your income you might find it to be a valuable experiment. Educational, if nothing else.
BTC sounds great, based on my limited knowledge! It hasn't caught on in My Old Kentucky Home though. I'm thinking Credit Union is the best way to go.
Been a part of my credit union for about 10 years now, and had a better experience with them than any bank prior.

I've been using Simple.com as my primary bank for probably a year now. There are virtually no fees (the only fee they will ever change you is if you don't touch your account for six month or something like that). If you do manage to go negative, yiu just can't use your card until you go positive again.

There are three downsides. One, there are no brick and mortar locations… it's on the Internet only. You can set it up for direct deposit and you can deposit checks using your phone's camera. Two, you don't get a check book. You can write checks, but you do it through the app or website and they mail them out. And three, you really need to have a smart phone. I know they have an ios app, and I'm almost positive they have an android app, not sure about any other mobile OSes.
2nd the credit union plug. Avoid wells Fargo At all costs.
